summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Ahmad Shah Bahadur, the Mughal emperor who was born in 1725 and died in 1775. It states that he succeeded his father Muhammad Shah as the 13th Mughal Emperor in 1748 at age 22. The note says the Mughal Empire was collapsing when he took power, and that his administrative weaknesses helped lead to the rise of the usurper Feroze Jung III.
one_line: Ahmad Shah Bahadur, the 13th Mughal Emperor who reigned from 1748 as the empire was collapsing, and whose weaknesses let Feroze Jung III usurp power.
key_facts: Ahmad Shah Bahadur was also known as Mirza Ahmad Shah and Mujahid-ud-Din Ahmad Shah Ghazi.
Ahmad Shah Bahadur was born on 23 December 1725.
Ahmad Shah Bahadur died on 1 January 1775.
Ahmad Shah Bahadur was born to Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah.
Ahmad Shah Bahadur succeeded his father Muhammad Shah to the throne in 1748.
Ahmad Shah Bahadur became the 13th Mughal Emperor in 1748 at the age of 22.
When Ahmad Shah Bahadur came to power, the Mughal Empire was collapsing.
The administrative weaknesses of Ahmad Shah Bahadur eventually led to the rise of the usurping Feroze Jung III.
